symptom: `alter module … add | set | drop jar dependency` reports success and mx check stays clean, but the module's Projects$ModuleSettings loses PackageId (Studio Pro's Module ID) and, on a Marketplace module, its Checksum, and EnableDetailedTroubleshooting flips from false to true.
cause: UpdateModuleSettings marshalled a fresh bson.M of the nine keys types.ModuleSettings models; the six it does not (PackageId, Checksum, ConvertedChecksum, OriginalPackageId, ModuleDependencies, EnableDetailedTroubleshooting) were absent, and canon.CompletePropertySets put the names back with metamodel defaults rather than the stored values. The default enableDetailedTroubleshooting is true, which is why a false came back true.
insight: **A completed property set looks like a carry and is not one.** The rewritten unit had every key Studio Pro writes, so a key-presence check passed; only comparing VALUES against the stored unit showed the loss, and only on a module whose values differ from the defaults — an app module made by mxcli or Studio Pro holds defaults everywhere but PackageId, so the reproduction has to be a Marketplace module (WorkflowCommons in ako/TestApp: a Checksum, a PackageId and troubleshooting off). The fix starts the document from the stored keys and overwrites only the modelled ones, rather than adding six more fields to the rebuild, so the next key Studio Pro adds is carried too. One writer only (cmd_modules.go is its sole caller); CreateModule still writes a new module without a PackageId, unmeasured against Studio Pro. Control: the extracted function ignoring the stored bytes fails the fixture test on Checksum, PackageId, EnableDetailedTroubleshooting, ConvertedChecksum and OriginalPackageId; end to end on a TestApp copy the jar statement now changes only JarDependencies and mx check (11.16.0 Beta) reports 0 errors.
